summary: Following an analyst review request, card C06220-K1 was investigated for an anomalous burst of three online Product C purchases totaling $2,166.71 between January 17 and January 19, 2017 (transactions 3660125, 3660126, and 3660127). These transactions sharply deviated from established cardholder history and were conducted through anonymous proxies using rotating, newly generated device profiles (D009715, D009718, and D009721) to evade device-fingerprint detection. Cross-card analysis revealed an identical coordinated fraud scheme emerging simultaneously across three peer cards belonging to unrelated customers (C05061-K1, C07925-K1, and C10553-K1) during January 2017. Card C06220-K1 also has five prior confirmed fraud cases in its record. The activity was confirmed as an undocumented coordinated multi-card fraud scheme, resulting in card blocking, connected card monitoring, and regulatory reporting.
open_question: Direct cardholder contact to confirm lack of authorization for transactions 3660125, 3660126, and 3660127, along with merchant-level shipping address and IP subnet data, would confirm the common point of compromise linking the peer cards.

waiting.why: R9 and 3a: coordinated abuse that fits no documented pattern
